name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q01 - Genetic diversity in Rauwolfia and crops

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Genetic diversity refers to variation at the genetic level within a single species over its distributional range, as seen in the potency and concentration of reserpine in Rauwolfia vomitoria.

Statement II: India has more than \(50,000\) genetically different strains of rice and \(1,000\) varieties of mango.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Genetic diversity represents intraspecific variation in genes across different populations or geographical ranges of a single species.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
The medicinal plant Rauwolfia vomitoria growing in different Himalayan ranges shows genetic variation in the potency and concentration of its active chemical reserpine, which is a classic example of genetic diversity. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
India possesses rich agricultural genetic diversity, including more than \(50,000\) genetically different strains of rice and \(1,000\) varieties of mango. Thus, the second claim is also true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements accurately describe facts and examples of genetic diversity.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q02 - IUCN species count and Robert May estimate

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: According to the IUCN (2004), the total number of plant and animal species described so far is slightly more than \(1.5\) million.

Statement II: Robert May's conservative and scientifically sound estimate places global species diversity at about \(50\) million.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Published species records quantify described species, whereas statistical extrapolations estimate the total number of species on Earth, including undiscovered ones.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) (2004), slightly more than \(1.5\) million plant and animal species have been described so far. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
While some extreme estimates range from \(20\) to \(50\) million, Robert May's conservative and scientifically sound estimate places global species diversity at about \(7\) million, not \(50\) million. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is correct while the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q03 - Global share of plants and insects

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise more than \(70\%\) of all recorded species on Earth.

Statement II: Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than \(70\%\) of the total animal species.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Global species inventories show that animals vastly outnumber plants in described species diversity.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
More than \(70\%\) of all recorded species are animals, whereas plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms, and angiosperms) comprise no more than \(22\%\) of the total. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Among animals, insects form the most species-rich taxonomic group, accounting for more than \(70\%\) of all animal species (about \(7\) out of every \(10\) animals). Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is incorrect while the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q04 - Prokaryotes in global biodiversity estimates

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Conventional taxonomic methods are well suited for identifying all prokaryotic species, and nearly all microbes are easily culturable under laboratory conditions.

Statement II: Standard global biodiversity estimates of \(1.5\) million described species and Robert May's \(7\) million estimate include complete figures for prokaryotes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Identifying and enumerating prokaryotic species poses fundamental methodological challenges compared to eukaryotic plants and animals.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Conventional taxonomic methods are not suitable for identifying microbial species, and many prokaryotic species are simply not culturable under laboratory conditions. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Standard global biodiversity inventories and Robert May's estimate do not give any figures for prokaryotes; using biochemical or molecular criteria, prokaryotic diversity alone might run into millions. Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q05 - India biodiversity share and recorded species

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Although India has only \(2.4\%\) of the world's land area, its share of global species diversity is an impressive \(8.1\%\).

Statement II: Nearly \(45,000\) species of plants and twice as many species of animals have been recorded from India.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India is one of the \(12\) mega diversity countries of the world due to its disproportionately high species richness relative to its land area.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
India occupies \(2.4\%\) of the world's land area yet accounts for \(8.1\%\) of global species diversity. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Nearly \(45,000\) plant species and roughly twice as many (around \(90,000\)) animal species have been recorded from India. Thus, the second claim is also true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q06 - Latitudinal gradient in bird diversity

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: In general, species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles.

Statement II: Greenland at \(71^\circ\text{ N}\) harbours more bird species than Colombia located near the equator.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The latitudinal gradient in biodiversity describes how species richness varies with latitude from the equator to polar regions.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Species diversity generally decreases as one moves away from the equator toward the poles, with tropical regions harbouring far more species than temperate or polar areas. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Colombia located near the equator has nearly \(1,400\) species of birds, whereas Greenland at \(71^\circ\text{ N}\) has only \(56\) species of birds. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is correct while the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q07 - Species-area relationship on arithmetic and log scales

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: In Alexander von Humboldt's species–area relationship, plotting species richness against area on an arithmetic scale yields a straight line.

Statement II: On a logarithmic scale, the species–area relationship is a straight line described by the equation \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alexander von Humboldt showed that within a region, species richness (\(S\)) increases with explored area (\(A\)) up to a limit according to \(S = CA^Z\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
On an arithmetic scale, the relationship \(S = CA^Z\) turns out to be a rectangular hyperbola, not a straight line. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Taking logarithms converts \(S = CA^Z\) into \(\log S = \log C + Z \log A\), which is a straight line on a log–log scale with slope \(Z\) and Y-intercept \(\log C\). Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is incorrect while the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q08 - David Tilman outdoor plot experiments

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: In David Tilman's long-term outdoor plot experiments, plots with more species showed greater year-to-year variation in total biomass.

Statement II: David Tilman also observed that increased species diversity contributed to lower productivity in his experimental plots.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
David Tilman's long-term ecosystem experiments tested how species richness affects community stability and biomass productivity.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass, indicating greater stability rather than greater variation. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Tilman also showed that increased diversity contributed to higher productivity, not lower productivity. Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q09 - IUCN Red List extinctions and threatened species

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of \(784\) species (including \(338\) vertebrates, \(359\) invertebrates, and \(87\) plants) in the last \(500\) years.

Statement II: More than \(15,500\) species worldwide are currently facing the threat of extinction.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Global conservation assessments track both documented historical extinctions and the number of extant species currently threatened with extinction.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
The IUCN Red List (2004) documents \(784\) species extinctions over the last \(500\) years, comprising \(338\) vertebrates, \(359\) invertebrates, and \(87\) plants. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
More than \(15,500\) species worldwide (including over \(650\) from India) currently face the threat of extinction. Thus, the second claim is also true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q10 - Habitat loss and tropical rain forest cover

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.

Statement II: Tropical rain forests currently cover more than \(14\%\) of the Earth's land surface.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Among 'The Evil Quartet' of biodiversity loss drivers, habitat destruction and fragmentation represent the primary threat to global species survival.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Habitat loss and fragmentation is indeed the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Tropical rain forests once covered more than \(14\%\) of Earth's land surface, but due to rapid deforestation they now cover no more than \(6\%\). Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is correct while the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q11 - Invasive species in Indian ecosystems

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: The illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture has helped increase the population of indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers.

Statement II: Parthenium (carrot grass), Lantana, and Eichhornia (water hyacinth) are native Indian plant species that protect ecosystems from alien invasions.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alien species introduced unintentionally or deliberately can become invasive, causing the decline or extinction of indigenous species.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
The recent illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus for aquaculture purposes poses a serious threat to indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers, rather than helping them. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Parthenium (carrot grass), Lantana, and Eichhornia (water hyacinth) are invasive alien weed species that cause severe environmental damage and threaten native species. Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q12 - Broadly utilitarian versus ethical arguments

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: The Amazon forest producing \(20\%\) of the total oxygen in Earth's atmosphere through photosynthesis represents a narrowly utilitarian argument for conserving biodiversity.

Statement II: The ethical argument for conserving biodiversity recognises that every species has an intrinsic value, even if it has no current or economic value to humans.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Conservation arguments are classified into narrowly utilitarian (direct economic products), broadly utilitarian (ecosystem services and aesthetic benefits), and ethical (intrinsic value and moral duty).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Oxygen production by the Amazon forest is a major ecosystem service provided by nature and falls under the broadly utilitarian argument, not the narrowly utilitarian argument. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
The ethical argument states that every species has an intrinsic value regardless of economic utility, and humans have a moral duty to care for their well-being. Thus, the second claim is true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is incorrect while the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q13 - Global biodiversity hotspots and India

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Initially \(25\) biodiversity hotspots were identified worldwide, and subsequently nine more were added, bringing the total to \(34\).

Statement II: Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya are the three biodiversity hotspots that cover India's exceptionally high biodiversity regions.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biodiversity hotspots are regions with very high species richness, high endemism, and accelerated habitat loss selected for priority in situ protection.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Initially \(25\) hotspots were identified globally, and \(9\) more were added later, making a total of \(34\) biodiversity hotspots. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
Three of these \(34\) hotspots—Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Himalaya—cover India's exceptionally high biodiversity regions. Thus, the second claim is also true.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q14 - Sacred groves and Indian protected areas

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: In Meghalaya, the sacred groves in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.

Statement II: India currently has \(90\) biosphere reserves, \(14\) national parks, and \(448\) wildlife sanctuaries.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India's in situ conservation comprises both legally protected areas (biosphere reserves, national parks, wildlife sanctuaries) and culturally protected sacred groves.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Sacred groves in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya serve as the last refuges for many rare and threatened plant species. Thus, the first claim is true.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
India has \(14\) biosphere reserves, \(90\) national parks, and \(448\) wildlife sanctuaries—the numbers for biosphere reserves and national parks are swapped in the second claim. Thus, the second claim is false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the first statement is correct while the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_STMT_Q15 - Ex situ methods and international summits

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option.

Statement I: Zoological parks, botanical gardens, and cryopreservation of gametes are examples of in situ conservation.

Statement II: At the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Rio de Janeiro in \(1992\), \(190\) countries pledged to significantly reduce biodiversity loss by \(2010\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ex situ conservation protects threatened organisms outside their natural habitats, while global conservation commitments were established through two distinct international summits.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Claim
Zoological parks, botanical gardens, and cryopreservation of gametes are classic methods of ex situ (off-site) conservation, not in situ conservation. Thus, the first claim is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Claim
The Earth Summit (Convention on Biological Diversity) was held in Rio de Janeiro in \(1992\), whereas the World Summit on Sustainable Development—where \(190\) countries pledged to reduce biodiversity loss by \(2010\)—was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in \(2002\). Thus, the second claim is also false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Therefore, both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
